hymns.title: What a Friend We Have in Jesus
hymns.story: Joseph Scriven wrote this as a poem to comfort his mother in Ireland after he had emigrated to Canada, following two devastating personal losses: his first fiancee drowned the night before their wedding, and years later his second fiancee died of illness before they could marry. He never intended it for publication; a friend found the poem while nursing him through an illness and had it printed anonymously. Charles Crozat Converse later wrote the tune.
hymns.lyrics:
What a friend we have in Jesus,
All our sins and griefs to bear!
What a privilege to carry
Everything to God in prayer!
Oh, what peace we often forfeit,
Oh, what needless pain we bear,
All because we do not carry
Everything to God in prayer!

Have we trials and temptations?
Is there trouble anywhere?
We should never be discouraged;
Take it to the Lord in prayer.
Can we find a friend so faithful
Who will all our sorrows share?
Jesus knows our every weakness;
Take it to the Lord in prayer.

Are we weak and heavy laden,
Cumbered with a load of care?
Precious Savior, still our refuge—
Take it to the Lord in prayer.
Do thy friends despise, forsake thee?
Take it to the Lord in prayer!
In His arms He'll take and shield thee,
Thou wilt find a solace there.

hymns.title: Sweet Hour of Prayer
hymns.author_composer: William W. Walford (words); William B. Bradbury (music)
hymns.story: William Walford was a blind English lay preacher who composed the words in his head and dictated them to a friend, Thomas Salmon, who later brought them to America. The hymn is a meditation on prayer as a refuge, and became one of the most beloved devotional hymns of the 19th century after Bradbury set it to music in 1861.
hymns.lyrics:
Sweet hour of prayer, sweet hour of prayer,
That calls me from a world of care,
And bids me at my Father's throne
Make all my wants and wishes known.
In seasons of distress and grief,
My soul has often found relief,
And oft escaped the tempter's snare,
By thy return, sweet hour of prayer.

Sweet hour of prayer, sweet hour of prayer,
The joys I feel, the bliss I share,
Of those whose anxious spirits burn
With strong desires for thy return!
With such I hasten to the place
Where God my Savior shows His face,
And gladly take my station there,
And wait for thee, sweet hour of prayer.

Sweet hour of prayer, sweet hour of prayer,
Thy wings shall my petition bear
To Him whose truth and faithfulness
Engage the waiting soul to bless.
And since He bids me seek His face,
Believe His word and trust His grace,
I'll cast on Him my every care,
And wait for thee, sweet hour of prayer.

hymns.title: Trust and Obey
hymns.author_composer: John H. Sammis (words); Daniel B. Towner (music)
hymns.story: This hymn grew out of a testimony meeting led by evangelist D. L. Moody. A young man stood and said, 'I am not quite sure, but I am going to trust, and I am going to obey.' Towner, who was present, jotted down the phrase and sent it to Sammis, a pastor, who turned it into the hymn's refrain. Note: the user listed this once as 'Just obey,' which appears to be this same hymn.
hymns.lyrics:
When we walk with the Lord
In the light of His Word,
What a glory He sheds on our way!
While we do His good will,
He abides with us still,
And with all who will trust and obey.

Trust and obey, for there's no other way
To be happy in Jesus, but to trust and obey.

Not a shadow can rise,
Not a cloud in the skies,
But His smile quickly drives it away;
Not a doubt or a fear,
Not a sigh or a tear,
Can abide while we trust and obey.

Not a burden we bear,
Not a sorrow we share,
But our toil He doth richly repay;
Not a grief or a loss,
Not a frown or a cross,
But is blest if we trust and obey.

Then in fellowship sweet
We will sit at His feet,
Or we'll walk by His side in the way;
What He says we will do,
Where He sends we will go,
Never fear, only trust and obey.

hymns.title: Higher Ground
hymns.story: Johnson Oatman Jr. was a Methodist lay preacher and prolific hymn writer (he wrote several thousand hymn texts) who often wrote about the Christian's pursuit of spiritual growth. 'Higher Ground' pictures the Christian life as a steady climb toward greater faith and holiness, set to music by Charles H. Gabriel.
hymns.lyrics:
I'm pressing on the upward way,
New heights I'm gaining every day;
Still praying as I onward bound,
'Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.'

Lord, lift me up and let me stand,
By faith, on Heaven's tableland,
A higher plane than I have found;
Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.

My heart has no desire to stay
Where doubts arise and fears dismay;
Though some may dwell where these abound,
My prayer, my aim, is higher ground.

I want to live above the world,
Though Satan's darts at me are hurled;
For faith has caught the joyful sound,
The song of saints on higher ground.

I want to scale the utmost height,
And catch a gleam of glory bright;
But still I'll pray till heav'n I've found,
'Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.'

hymns.title: 'Tis So Sweet to Trust in Jesus
hymns.author_composer: Louisa M. R. Stead (words); William J. Kirkpatrick (music)
hymns.story: Louisa Stead wrote this hymn out of profound grief. According to tradition, she witnessed her husband drown while trying to save a boy at a beach outing, leaving her a widow with a young daughter. In the midst of that loss she wrote of resting simply in the trustworthiness of Jesus, a theme that has comforted grieving believers ever since.
hymns.lyrics:
'Tis so sweet to trust in Jesus,
Just to take Him at His word;
Just to rest upon His promise,
Just to know, 'Thus saith the Lord.'

Jesus, Jesus, how I trust Him,
How I've proved Him o'er and o'er;
Jesus, Jesus, precious Jesus!
O for grace to trust Him more!

O how sweet to trust in Jesus,
Just to trust His cleansing blood;
Just in simple faith to plunge me
'Neath the healing, cleansing flood!

Yes, 'tis sweet to trust in Jesus,
Just from sin and self to cease;
Just from Jesus simply taking
Life and rest, and joy and peace.

I'm so glad I learned to trust Thee,
Precious Jesus, Savior, Friend;
And I know that Thou art with me,
Wilt be with me to the end.

hymns.title: Faith of Our Fathers
hymns.story: Frederick Faber, a convert to Catholicism from Anglicanism, wrote this in tribute to English Catholics who were persecuted for their faith. Protestant hymnals later adapted the lyrics ('Faith of our fathers, holy faith' replacing references specific to Rome) so that it became a widely sung hymn across many denominations, often associated with steadfastness under trial.
hymns.lyrics:
Faith of our fathers, living still
In spite of dungeon, fire, and sword;
O how our hearts beat high with joy
Whenever we hear that glorious Word!

Faith of our fathers, holy faith!
We will be true to thee till death.

Our fathers, chained in prisons dark,
Were still in heart and conscience free;
How sweet would be their children's fate,
If they, like them, could die for thee!

Faith of our fathers, we will strive
To win all nations unto thee;
And through the truth that comes from God,
Mankind shall then indeed be free.

Faith of our fathers, we will love
Both friend and foe in all our strife;
And preach thee, too, as love knows how,
By kindly words and virtuous life.

hymns.title: I Surrender All
hymns.author_composer: Judson W. Van DeVenter (words); Winfield S. Weeden (music)
hymns.story: Van DeVenter was a talented artist who felt torn between a career in art and a call to evangelistic ministry. He wrote that for five years he struggled with 'a great conflict and a great crisis' until he finally surrendered his own plans, and this hymn came from that decision to give his life fully over to God's direction.
hymns.lyrics:
All to Jesus, I surrender,
All to Him I freely give;
I will ever love and trust Him,
In His presence daily live.

I surrender all, I surrender all,
All to Thee, my blessed Savior,
I surrender all.

All to Jesus I surrender,
Humbly at His feet I bow,
Worldly pleasures all forsaken;
Take me, Jesus, take me now.

All to Jesus I surrender,
Make me, Savior, wholly Thine;
Let me feel the Holy Spirit,
Truly know that Thou art mine.

All to Jesus I surrender,
Lord, I give myself to Thee;
Fill me with Thy love and power,
Let Thy blessing fall on me.

All to Jesus I surrender,
Now I feel the sacred flame.
O the joy of full salvation!
Glory, glory, to His Name!

hymns.title: Oh, to Be Like Thee
hymns.story: Thoro Harris was a hymn writer and musician associated with the American holiness movement. This hymn is a heartfelt prayer of consecration, expressing the believer's longing to be conformed to the character of Christ rather than simply admiring Him from a distance.
hymns.lyrics:
Oh, to be like Thee! blessed Redeemer,
This is my constant longing and prayer;
Gladly I'll forfeit all of earth's treasures,
Jesus, Thy perfect likeness to wear.

Oh, to be like Thee! oh, to be like Thee,
Blessed Redeemer, pure as Thou art;
Come in Thy sweetness, come in Thy fullness;
Stamp Thine own image deep on my heart.

Oh, to be like Thee! full of compassion,
Loving, forgiving, tender and kind,
Helping the helpless, cheering the fainting,
Seeking the wandering sinner to find.

Oh, to be like Thee! lowly in spirit,
Holy and harmless, patient and brave;
Meekly enduring cruel reproaches,
Willing to suffer others to save.

Oh, to be like Thee! while I am pleading,
Pour out Thy Spirit, fill with Thy love;
Make me a temple meet for Thy dwelling,
Fit me for life and heaven above.

hymns.title: Draw Me Nearer (I Am Thine, O Lord)
hymns.author_composer: Fanny J. Crosby (words); William H. Doane (music)
hymns.story: Fanny Crosby, the prolific blind hymn writer, penned this as a prayer of intimate communion with God, envisioning prayer as the place where the believer draws close to the divine presence. It was written for and set to music by her frequent collaborator William Doane.
hymns.lyrics:
I am Thine, O Lord, I have heard Thy voice,
And it told Thy love to me;
But I long to rise in the arms of faith
And be closer drawn to Thee.

Draw me nearer, nearer, blessed Lord,
To the cross where Thou hast died;
Draw me nearer, nearer, nearer, blessed Lord,
To Thy precious, bleeding side.

Consecrate me now to Thy service, Lord,
By the power of grace divine;
Let my soul look up with a steadfast hope,
And my will be lost in Thine.

O the pure delight of a single hour
That before Thy throne I spend,
When I kneel in prayer, and with Thee, my God,
I commune as friend with friend!

There are depths of love that I cannot know
Till I cross the narrow sea;
There are heights of joy that I may not reach
Till I rest in peace with Thee.

hymns.title: Close to Thee
hymns.author_composer: Fanny J. Crosby (words); Silas J. Vail (music)
hymns.story: Another of Fanny Crosby's devotional texts, this hymn expresses a simple, steady desire to stay near to Christ through all of life's circumstances, ending in the hope of eternal nearness to Him in heaven.
hymns.lyrics:
Thou my everlasting portion,
More than friend or life to me,
All along my pilgrim journey,
Savior, let me walk with Thee.

Close to Thee, close to Thee,
Close to Thee, close to Thee;
All along my pilgrim journey,
Savior, let me walk with Thee.

Not for ease or worldly pleasure,
Nor for fame my prayer shall be;
Gladly will I toil and suffer,
Only let me walk with Thee.

Lead me through the vale of shadows,
Bear me o'er life's fitful sea;
Then the gate of life eternal
May I enter, Lord, with Thee.

hymns.title: I Need Thee Every Hour
hymns.author_composer: Annie S. Hawks (words); Robert Lowry (music, refrain)
hymns.story: Annie Hawks wrote that the words came to her suddenly while doing housework, in a moment of simple joy in God's presence rather than crisis. Ironically, the hymn's full meaning of dependence on God became real to her only later, when she experienced deep grief after her husband's death.

hymns.title: Have You Been to Jesus (for the Cleansing Power)
hymns.story: Elisha Hoffman was a minister and hymn writer who wrote hundreds of gospel songs, often on themes of assurance and cleansing from sin. This hymn asks the listener directly whether they have come to Christ to be washed 'in the blood of the Lamb,' a favorite invitation hymn at revival meetings.
hymns.lyrics:
Have you been to Jesus for the cleansing power?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?
Are you fully trusting in His grace this hour?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?

Are you washed in the blood,
In the soul-cleansing blood of the Lamb?
Are your garments spotless? Are they white as snow?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?

Are you walking daily by the Savior's side?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?
Do you rest each moment in the Crucified?
Are you washed in the blood of the Lamb?

When the Bridegroom cometh will your robes be white,
Pure and white in the blood of the Lamb?
Will your soul be ready for the mansions bright,
And be washed in the blood of the Lamb?

Lay aside the garments that are stained with sin,
And be washed in the blood of the Lamb;
There's a fountain flowing for the soul unclean,
O be washed in the blood of the Lamb!

hymns.title: I Have Decided to Follow Jesus
hymns.author_composer: Traditional (origin attributed to a convert in Northeast India / Assam)
hymns.story: According to widely repeated tradition, this song's words come from a young convert in India (often placed in the Garo Hills/Assam region) who was martyred for his newfound Christian faith after his family threatened him if he would not recant. It has since become a well-loved commitment hymn worldwide, though the exact historical details of its origin are not fully documented.

hymns.title: The Solid Rock (My Hope Is Built)
hymns.story: Edward Mote was a carpenter by trade who said he wrote a few lines each morning on his way to work, inspired by a sermon on Christ as the foundation of faith. He later became a pastor and gave the hymn to a dying woman for comfort, only to discover neither of them owned a hymnbook containing it, which spurred him to publish it.
hymns.lyrics:
My hope is built on nothing less
Than Jesus' blood and righteousness;
I dare not trust the sweetest frame,
But wholly lean on Jesus' name.

On Christ, the solid Rock, I stand;
All other ground is sinking sand,
All other ground is sinking sand.

When darkness veils His lovely face,
I rest on His unchanging grace;
In every high and stormy gale,
My anchor holds within the veil.

His oath, His covenant, His blood,
Support me in the whelming flood;
When all around my soul gives way,
He then is all my hope and stay.

When He shall come with trumpet sound,
Oh, may I then in Him be found,
Dressed in His righteousness alone,
Faultless to stand before the throne.

hymns.title: Blessed Assurance
hymns.author_composer: Fanny J. Crosby (words); Phoebe P. Knapp (music)
hymns.story: According to Fanny Crosby's own account, her friend Phoebe Knapp played a new melody for her on the piano and asked what it said to her; Crosby immediately replied, 'Blessed assurance, Jesus is mine,' and the rest of the text followed. It has become one of the most famous hymns of personal assurance of salvation.
hymns.lyrics:
Blessed assurance, Jesus is mine!
Oh, what a foretaste of glory divine!
Heir of salvation, purchase of God,
Born of His Spirit, washed in His blood.

This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Savior all the day long;
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Savior all the day long.

Perfect submission, perfect delight,
Visions of rapture now burst on my sight;
Angels descending bring from above
Echoes of mercy, whispers of love.

Perfect submission, all is at rest,
I in my Savior am happy and blest,
Watching and waiting, looking above,
Filled with His goodness, lost in His love.

hymns.title: Fill My Cup, Lord
hymns.story: Richard Blanchard wrote this hymn drawing on the story of the Samaritan woman at the well in John 4, using her request for living water as a picture of the soul's thirst that only God can satisfy. It remains a favorite invitation and communion hymn in many churches today.
hymns.note: Still under copyright (Word Music/Richard Blanchard, 1959) - full lyrics not reproduced; the story above is original summary.

hymns.title: He Touched Me
hymns.story: Bill Gaither wrote this after hearing gospel singer Dottie Rambo's 'He Touched Me' theme resonate with his own testimony of personal transformation. It became one of the signature songs of the Gaithers and of Southern gospel music, describing the moment Christ's touch changed the writer's life.
hymns.note: Still under copyright (Gaither Music Company, 1963) - full lyrics not reproduced.

hymns.title: Heaven Came Down
hymns.story: John W. Peterson, a prolific 20th-century gospel songwriter, wrote this celebratory testimony hymn about the moment of conversion, when he says 'glory filled my soul' - describing salvation as heaven breaking into an ordinary life.
hymns.note: Still under copyright (John W. Peterson Music Company, 1961) - full lyrics not reproduced.

hymns.title: Will Your Anchor Hold
hymns.author_composer: Priscilla J. Owens (words); William J. Kirkpatrick (music)
hymns.story: Priscilla Owens was a Baltimore schoolteacher and Sunday school hymn writer. Drawing on Hebrews 6:19 ('hope as an anchor of the soul'), she pictured the Christian life as a ship anchored securely in Christ through the storms of life.
hymns.lyrics:
Will your anchor hold in the storms of life,
When the clouds unfold their wings of strife?
When the strong tides lift, and the cables strain,
Will your anchor drift, or firm remain?

We have an anchor that keeps the soul
Steadfast and sure while the billows roll,
Fastened to the Rock which cannot move,
Grounded firm and deep in the Savior's love.

It is safely moored, 'twill the storm withstand,
For 'tis well secured by the Savior's hand;
And the cables passed from His heart to mine,
Can defy the blast, through strength divine.

It will surely hold in the straits of fear,
When the breakers have told the reef is near;
Though the tempest rave and the wild winds blow,
Not an angry wave shall our bark o'erflow.

It will firmly hold in the floods of death,
When the waters cold chill our latest breath,
On the rising tide it can never fail,
While our hopes abide within the veil.

hymns.title: Leave It There
hymns.story: Charles Tindley was a self-taught African American Methodist minister in Philadelphia whose gospel songs, born out of the struggles of his congregation, deeply shaped the emerging tradition of American gospel music. 'Leave It There' encourages believers to bring every burden and injustice to God and trust Him to work it out, rather than carrying it alone.

hymns.title: Let Others See Jesus in You
hymns.story: B. B. McKinney was a Southern Baptist music leader and hymn writer whose songs urged believers toward practical, visible holiness. This hymn is a prayer that one's daily conduct - kindness, patience, honesty - would clearly reflect Christ to others.
hymns.lyrics:
Oh, brother, do you know the Savior,
Who is wondrous kind and true?
He's the fairest of ten thousand;
Let others see Jesus in you.

Let others see Jesus in you,
Let others see Jesus in you;
Keep telling the story, be faithful and true;
Let others see Jesus in you.

Do you tell the world about Him?
Does your light burn clear and true?
Is your life a real epistle,
That all men may read and construe?

Do you show the tender patience
Of the Lord you love and serve?
Do you walk in genuine meekness,
Merciful and undeserved?

hymns.title: Must I Go, and Empty-Handed?
hymns.author_composer: Charles C. Luther (words); George C. Stebbins (music)
hymns.story: Written in the era of camp meetings and revivalism, this hymn asks whether a believer will stand before Christ with nothing to show for their life and witness - no souls led to Him - and urges present, active service and evangelism.
hymns.lyrics:
Must I go, and empty-handed,
Thus my dear Redeemer meet?
Not one day of service give Him,
Lay no trophy at His feet?

Must I go, and empty-handed?
Must I meet my Savior so?
Not one soul with which to greet Him:
Must I empty-handed go?

Not at death I shrink or falter,
For my Savior saves me now;
But to meet Him empty-handed,
Thought of that now clouds my brow.

O the years in sinning wasted,
Could I but recall them now,
I would give them to my Savior,
To His will I'd gladly bow.

O ye saints, arouse, be earnest,
Up and work while yet 'tis day;
Ere the night of death o'ertake thee,
Strive for souls while still you may.

hymns.title: Nothing but the Blood of Jesus
hymns.story: Robert Lowry was a Baptist pastor and hymn composer who wrote both words and music for many gospel songs. This hymn insists that no human effort - good works, tears, prayers - can wash away sin; only the atoning blood of Christ can, a strong statement of the doctrine of salvation by grace alone.
hymns.lyrics:
What can wash away my sin?
Nothing but the blood of Jesus;
What can make me whole again?
Nothing but the blood of Jesus.

Oh! precious is the flow
That makes me white as snow;
No other fount I know,
Nothing but the blood of Jesus.

For my pardon, this I see,
Nothing but the blood of Jesus;
For my cleansing this my plea,
Nothing but the blood of Jesus.

Nothing can for sin atone,
Nothing but the blood of Jesus;
Naught of good that I have done,
Nothing but the blood of Jesus.

This is all my hope and peace,
Nothing but the blood of Jesus;
This is all my righteousness,
Nothing but the blood of Jesus.

hymns.title: O Jesus, I Have Promised
hymns.story: John Bode, an English clergyman, wrote this hymn for the confirmation of his own children, expressing a young believer's vow to remain faithful and close to Christ throughout life, guided and protected by Him amid the world's temptations.

hymns.title: Onward, Christian Soldiers
hymns.story: Sabine Baring-Gould, an English clergyman, wrote this in about fifteen minutes for a children's procession between villages on a festival day, intending it as a simple marching song for the children rather than a formal hymn. Arthur Sullivan (of Gilbert and Sullivan fame) later composed the well-known tune, and it became a staple processional and missionary hymn.
hymns.lyrics:
Onward, Christian soldiers, marching as to war,
With the cross of Jesus going on before.
Christ, the royal Master, leads against the foe;
Forward into battle see His banners go!

Onward, Christian soldiers, marching as to war,
With the cross of Jesus going on before.

At the sign of triumph Satan's host doth flee;
On then, Christian soldiers, on to victory!
Hell's foundations quiver at the shout of praise;
Brothers, lift your voices, loud your anthems raise.

Like a mighty army moves the Church of God;
Brothers, we are treading where the saints have trod.
We are not divided, all one body we,
One in hope and doctrine, one in charity.

Crowns and thrones may perish, kingdoms rise and wane,
But the Church of Jesus constant will remain.
Gates of hell can never gainst that Church prevail;
We have Christ's own promise, and that cannot fail.

Onward, then, ye people, join our happy throng,
Blend with ours your voices in the triumph song.
Glory, laud, and honor unto Christ the King,
This through countless ages men and angels sing.

hymns.title: Power in the Blood
hymns.story: Lewis Jones wrote both the words and music of this energetic gospel song about the redeeming and cleansing power found in the blood of Christ. Its rousing chorus made it a favorite at camp meetings and revivals.

hymns.title: Pentecostal Power
hymns.story: Charles H. Gabriel was one of the most prolific gospel songwriters of his era, often publishing under pen names such as 'Charlotte G. Homer.' This hymn is a fervent prayer for a fresh outpouring of the Holy Spirit, echoing the revivalist longing of early 20th-century American churches for the 'old-time power' of the Book of Acts.
hymns.lyrics:
Lord, as of old at Pentecost
Thou didst Thy power display,
With cleansing, purifying flame,
Descend on us today.

Lord, send the old-time power,
The Pentecostal power!
Thy floodgates of blessing on us throw open wide!
Lord, send the old-time power, the Pentecostal power,
That sinners be converted and Thy name glorified!

For mighty works for Thee, prepare
And strengthen every heart;
Come, take possession of Thine own,
And never more depart.

All self consume, all sin destroy!
With earnest zeal endue
Each waiting heart to work for Thee;
O Lord, our faith renew!

Speak, Lord! before Thy throne we wait,
Thy promise we believe,
And will not let Thee go until
The blessing we receive.

hymns.title: Rescue the Perishing
hymns.author_composer: Fanny J. Crosby (words); William H. Doane (music)
hymns.story: Fanny Crosby wrote this after visiting a mission in a rough part of New York City, where she was moved by the plight of the poor and spiritually lost. She addressed it directly to Christian workers, urging them to actively seek out and care for those who feel forgotten or beyond hope.

hymns.title: Show a Little Bit of Love and Kindness
hymns.story: I couldn't confidently identify this exact hymn title - it may be a lesser-known chorus or gospel song rather than a standard hymnal entry.
hymns.note: Please confirm the source/author if you have it, or let me know if this is a chorus from a specific songbook.

hymns.title: To God Be the Glory
hymns.author_composer: Fanny J. Crosby (words); William H. Doane (music)
hymns.story: Written by Fanny Crosby, this hymn was not especially popular in America at first, but it became widely beloved after evangelist Billy Graham's team, especially singer Cliff Barrows, revived it during crusades in Britain in the 1950s, after which it spread back into common use worldwide.
hymns.lyrics:
To God be the glory, great things He hath done;
So loved He the world that He gave us His Son,
Who yielded His life an atonement for sin,
And opened the life-gate that all may go in.

Praise the Lord, praise the Lord, let the earth hear His voice!
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord, let the people rejoice!
O come to the Father, through Jesus the Son,
And give Him the glory, great things He hath done.

O perfect redemption, the purchase of blood,
To every believer the promise of God;
The vilest offender who truly believes,
That moment from Jesus a pardon receives.

Great things He hath taught us, great things He hath done,
And great our rejoicing through Jesus the Son;
But purer, and higher, and greater will be
Our wonder, our transport, when Jesus we see.

hymns.title: Wash Me, O Lamb of God (Whiter Than Snow)
hymns.story: James Nicholson's hymn, based on Psalm 51:7 ('wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow'), is a direct prayer for inward cleansing from sin, commonly known by its refrain 'Whiter Than Snow.'

hymns.title: Where Could I Go (but to the Lord)
hymns.story: This Southern gospel favorite reflects on having nowhere else to turn but to God amid life's trials and heartaches. Depending on the exact publication date and renewal status, it may still be under copyright protection through Southern gospel publishers.
hymns.note: Composed 1940 by James B. Coats - copyright status uncertain to me; likely still restricted. Lyrics not reproduced out of caution.

hymns.title: Yield Not to Temptation
hymns.story: Horatio Palmer, a music educator and composer, wrote this as an encouragement especially to young people to resist temptation by relying on God's strength and the help of Jesus, rather than their own willpower alone.

hymns.title: There Shall Be Showers of Blessing
hymns.story: Based on Ezekiel 34:26, this hymn by Elisha Hoffman promises that God will send spiritual refreshing ('showers of blessing') on those who seek Him, a favorite theme in the revivalist gospel songs of the late 1800s.
hymns.lyrics:
There shall be showers of blessing:
This is the promise of love;
There shall be seasons refreshing,
Sent from the Savior above.

Showers of blessing, showers of blessing we need:
Mercy drops round us are falling,
But for the showers we plead.

There shall be showers of blessing,
Precious reviving again;
Over the hills and the valleys,
Sound of abundance of rain.

There shall be showers of blessing;
Send them upon us, O Lord;
Grant to us now a refreshing,
Come, and now honor Thy Word.

There shall be showers of blessing;
Oh, that today they might fall,
Now as to God we're confessing,
Now as on Jesus we call!

hymns.title: When the Roll Is Called Up Yonder
hymns.story: James Black, a Sunday school teacher, was inspired to write this after a teenage girl in his class missed roll call one day; it struck him how names are called on earth, which led him to think of the final roll call in heaven. The girl later died young, adding poignancy to the hymn.
hymns.lyrics:
When the trumpet of the Lord shall sound, and time shall be no more,
And the morning breaks, eternal, bright and fair;
When the saved of earth shall gather over on the other shore,
And the roll is called up yonder, I'll be there.

When the roll is called up yonder,
When the roll is called up yonder,
When the roll is called up yonder,
When the roll is called up yonder, I'll be there.

On that bright and cloudless morning when the dead in Christ shall rise,
And the glory of His resurrection share;
When His chosen ones shall gather to their home beyond the skies,
And the roll is called up yonder, I'll be there.

Let us labor for the Master from the dawn till setting sun,
Let us talk of all His wondrous love and care;
Then when all of life is over, and our work on earth is done,
And the roll is called up yonder, I'll be there.

hymns.title: I Must Tell Jesus
hymns.story: Elisha Hoffman wrote this after visiting and comforting a woman burdened by grief who had no one else to turn to; he encouraged her to tell it all to Jesus, and the phrase stayed with him and became this well-loved hymn of bringing every sorrow directly to Christ.

hymns.title: Pass Me Not, O Gentle Savior
hymns.author_composer: Fanny J. Crosby (words); William H. Doane (music)
hymns.story: Fanny Crosby based this hymn on the biblical story of blind Bartimaeus, who cried out to Jesus for mercy and refused to be silenced. Her own blindness gave the plea 'pass me not' a personal resonance, as a heartfelt cry to not be overlooked by the Savior.
hymns.lyrics:
Pass me not, O gentle Savior,
Hear my humble cry;
While on others Thou art calling,
Do not pass me by.

Savior, Savior, hear my humble cry;
While on others Thou art calling,
Do not pass me by.

Let me at Thy throne of mercy
Find a sweet relief,
Kneeling there in deep contrition;
Help my unbelief.

Trusting only in Thy merit,
Would I seek Thy face;
Heal my wounded, broken spirit,
Save me by Thy grace.

Thou the spring of all my comfort,
More than life to me,
Whom have I on earth beside Thee?
Whom in heaven but Thee?

hymns.title: Have You Counted the Cost
hymns.story: This gospel hymn draws on Luke 14, where Jesus urges would-be disciples to first count the cost of following Him, warning against half-hearted commitment and urging complete surrender to Christ.
hymns.lyrics:
Have you counted the cost, if your soul should be lost,
Though you gain the whole world for your own?
Even now it may be that the line you have crossed,
Have you counted, have you counted the cost?

Have you counted the cost? Have you counted the cost?
Even now it may be that the line you have crossed;
Have you counted, have you counted the cost?

hymns.title: The Great Judgment Morning
hymns.author_composer: James McGranahan (words and music, adapting an earlier text)
hymns.story: This solemn gospel song pictures a dramatic vision of the final judgment, warning sinners of the seriousness of standing unprepared before God, a common theme in 19th-century revival preaching and song.
hymns.lyrics:
A great and glorious morning
Dawns bright at last for me,
An endless life of glory
I in that morn shall see;
O joyful day, when free from sin
I shall my Savior see!

O that will be joyful, joyful, joyful,
O that will be joyful, when we meet to part no more;
O that will be joyful, joyful, joyful,
When we meet on Canaan's shore.
hymns.note: Well-known chorus reproduced with reasonable confidence; verses vary by hymnal and I'd recommend cross-checking full stanza set against Hymnary.org.

hymns.title: The Old Rugged Cross
hymns.story: George Bennard, a Methodist evangelist, said the hymn came to him gradually over months as he wrestled with what the cross truly meant, eventually completing it while preparing for a series of revival meetings in Michigan. It became one of the most enduring hymns in American Christianity.
hymns.lyrics:
On a hill far away stood an old rugged cross,
The emblem of suffering and shame;
And I love that old cross where the dearest and best
For a world of lost sinners was slain.

So I'll cherish the old rugged cross,
Till my trophies at last I lay down;
I will cling to the old rugged cross,
And exchange it some day for a crown.

Oh, that old rugged cross, so despised by the world,
Has a wondrous attraction for me;
For the dear Lamb of God left His glory above
To bear it to dark Calvary.

In that old rugged cross, stained with blood so divine,
A wondrous beauty I see,
For 'twas on that old cross Jesus suffered and died,
To pardon and sanctify me.

To the old rugged cross I will ever be true,
Its shame and reproach gladly bear;
Then He'll call me some day to my home far away,
Where His glory forever I'll share.

hymns.title: In Times Like These
hymns.story: Ruth Caye Jones reportedly wrote this hymn of steadfast trust in God during the uncertainty of World War II, urging believers to build their lives on the 'Solid Rock' amid a shaking, unstable world.
hymns.note: Published 1944 - likely still under copyright (renewal era); lyrics not reproduced out of caution, though the story is safe to share.

hymns.title: At the Cross
hymns.story: Isaac Watts, often called the father of English hymnody, wrote the original verses ('Alas! And Did My Savior Bleed') in the early 1700s as a meditation on Christ's crucifixion. Ralph Hudson later added the well-known refrain 'At the cross, at the cross' during the American revival era, and the combined hymn became a gospel standard.
hymns.lyrics:
Alas! and did my Savior bleed?
And did my Sovereign die?
Would He devote that sacred head
For such a worm as I?

At the cross, at the cross where I first saw the light,
And the burden of my heart rolled away,
It was there by faith I received my sight,
And now I am happy all the day!

Was it for crimes that I had done
He groaned upon the tree?
Amazing pity! grace unknown!
And love beyond degree!

Well might the sun in darkness hide,
And shut his glories in,
When God, the mighty Maker, died
For man the creature's sin.

Thus might I hide my blushing face
While His dear cross appears,
Dissolve my heart in thankfulness,
And melt mine eyes to tears.

But drops of grief can ne'er repay
The debt of love I owe;
Here, Lord, I give myself away,
'Tis all that I can do.

hymns.title: Rock of Ages, Cleft for Me
hymns.story: Legend holds that Augustus Toplady, an English clergyman, was caught in a sudden storm in a gorge and sheltered in the cleft of a large rock, which inspired the hymn's imagery, though this story is not fully verified. The hymn is a profound statement that salvation rests entirely on Christ, not on personal merit.
hymns.lyrics:
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee;
Let the water and the blood,
From Thy wounded side which flowed,
Be of sin the double cure,
Save from wrath and make me pure.

Not the labor of my hands
Can fulfill Thy law's demands;
Could my zeal no respite know,
Could my tears forever flow,
All for sin could not atone;
Thou must save, and Thou alone.

Nothing in my hand I bring,
Simply to Thy cross I cling;
Naked, come to Thee for dress;
Helpless, look to Thee for grace;
Foul, I to the fountain fly;
Wash me, Savior, or I die.

While I draw this fleeting breath,
When mine eyes shall close in death,
When I soar to worlds unknown,
See Thee on Thy judgment throne,
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee.

hymns.title: Grace Greater Than Our Sin
hymns.author_composer: Julia H. Johnston (words); Daniel B. Towner (music)
hymns.story: Julia Johnston was a Sunday school teacher and hymn writer whose text celebrates the overwhelming abundance of God's grace, able to cover sin no matter how great. Towner, a frequent collaborator with evangelist D. L. Moody's ministry, composed the tune.
hymns.lyrics:
Marvelous grace of our loving Lord,
Grace that exceeds our sin and our guilt!
Yonder on Calvary's mount outpoured,
There where the blood of the Lamb was spilt.

Grace, grace, God's grace,
Grace that will pardon and cleanse within;
Grace, grace, God's grace,
Grace that is greater than all our sin!

Sin and despair, like the sea waves cold,
Threaten the soul with infinite loss;
Grace that is greater, yes, grace untold,
Points to the refuge, the mighty cross.

Dark is the stain that we cannot hide,
What can avail to wash it away?
Look! there is flowing a crimson tide,
Whiter than snow you may be today.

Marvelous, infinite, matchless grace,
Freely bestowed on all who believe!
You that are longing to see His face,
Will you this moment His grace receive?

hymns.title: In the Sweet By and By
hymns.author_composer: Sanford F. Bennett (words); Joseph P. Webster (music)
hymns.story: According to Bennett's own account, his friend Webster was in a gloomy mood one day, so Bennett dashed off some comforting verses about the joys of heaven; Webster immediately set them to music, and the whole hymn was composed within about half an hour.
hymns.lyrics:
There's a land that is fairer than day,
And by faith we can see it afar;
For the Father waits over the way
To prepare us a dwelling place there.

In the sweet by and by,
We shall meet on that beautiful shore;
In the sweet by and by,
We shall meet on that beautiful shore.

We shall sing on that beautiful shore
The melodious songs of the blest,
And our spirits shall sorrow no more,
Not a sigh for the blessing of rest.

To our bountiful Father above,
We will offer our tribute of praise
For the glorious gift of His love
And the blessings that hallow our days.

hymns.title: Farther Along
hymns.author_composer: W. B. Stevens (attributed); traditional American gospel
hymns.story: This Southern gospel/country gospel standard reflects on the unanswered question of why the righteous often suffer while the wicked seem to prosper, and comforts the singer with the promise that understanding will come 'farther along' in life or in eternity.
hymns.lyrics:
Tempted and tried, we're oft made to wonder
Why it should be thus all the day long,
While there are others living about us,
Never molested, though in the wrong.

Farther along we'll know all about it,
Farther along we'll understand why;
Cheer up, my brother, live in the sunshine,
We'll understand it all by and by.

When death has come and taken our loved ones,
It leaves our home so lonely and drear;
Then do we wonder why others prosper,
Living so wicked year after year.

Faithful, unyielding, verses and cheerful,
Live on for Jesus, come joy or grief;
He knoweth best when He shall come and take us
Home to that mansion, prepared for us.
hymns.note: This is a traditional folk/gospel hymn with disputed/uncertain sole authorship; verse wording varies between hymnals.

hymns.title: Wandering Child, O Come Home
hymns.author_composer: Will L. Thompson (also known as 'Softly and Tenderly Jesus Is Calling')
hymns.story: Will Thompson wrote this hymn ('Softly and Tenderly') as a tender invitation to prodigal, wandering sinners to return home to God. It is said that evangelist D. L. Moody, on his deathbed, told Thompson he would rather have written this hymn than anything else in his life.
hymns.lyrics:
Softly and tenderly Jesus is calling,
Calling for you and for me;
See, on the portals He's waiting and watching,
Watching for you and for me.

Come home, come home,
You who are weary, come home;
Earnestly, tenderly, Jesus is calling,
Calling, O sinner, come home!

Why should we tarry when Jesus is pleading,
Pleading for you and for me?
Why should we linger and heed not His mercies,
Mercies for you and for me?

Time is now fleeting, the moments are passing,
Passing from you and from me;
Shadows are gathering, deathbeds are coming,
Coming for you and for me.

O for the wonderful love He has promised,
Promised for you and for me!
Though we have sinned, He has mercy and pardon,
Pardon for you and for me.
hymns.note: Listed by the user as 'Wandering Child, O Come Home' - this matches the theme/refrain of Will Thompson's well-known hymn 'Softly and Tenderly Jesus Is Calling'; flagging in case a different specific hymn was intended.

hymns.title: Come, Ye Sinners, Poor and Needy (Come Believing)
hymns.story: Joseph Hart was an English pastor who, after years of religious doubt and personal struggle, experienced a deep conversion and began writing hymns of grace and invitation to the spiritually needy. 'Come, ye sinners' invites those who feel unworthy to come to Christ just as they are.
hymns.lyrics:
Come, ye sinners, poor and needy,
Weak and wounded, sick and sore;
Jesus ready stands to save you,
Full of pity, love, and power.

I will arise and go to Jesus,
He will embrace me in His arms;
In the arms of my dear Savior,
Oh, there are ten thousand charms.

Come, ye thirsty, come, and welcome,
God's free bounty glorify;
True belief and true repentance,
Every grace that brings you nigh.

Let not conscience make you linger,
Nor of fitness fondly dream;
All the fitness He requireth
Is to feel your need of Him.

Agonizing in the garden,
Your Redeemer prostrate lies;
On the bloody tree behold Him,
Hear Him cry before He dies.
hymns.note: Listed as 'Come Believing' - matched to the well-known hymn 'Come, Ye Sinners, Poor and Needy,' whose refrain is sometimes titled by that phrase; flag if a different song was intended.

hymns.title: Search Me, O God
hymns.story: J. Edwin Orr, a revivalist and historian, adapted this hymn (based on a Maori melody, 'Whakaaria Mai') while attending a revival convention in New Zealand, as a heartfelt prayer of self-examination drawn from Psalm 139.
hymns.note: Composed 1936 - likely still under copyright; lyrics not reproduced out of caution.

hymns.title: Take Time to Be Holy
hymns.author_composer: William D. Longstaff (words); George C. Stebbins (music)
hymns.story: William Longstaff, a wealthy English layman, wrote this hymn reportedly after hearing a sermon on 'Be ye holy,' urging believers toward unhurried, disciplined spiritual devotion rather than a rushed or superficial faith.

hymns.title: Another Year Is Dawning
hymns.story: Frances Havergal, a devoted English hymn writer, wrote this as a New Year's prayer of consecration, dedicating each coming year - its joys and trials alike - fully into God's keeping.

hymns.title: Wonderful Story of Love
hymns.story: This hymn retells the 'wonderful story' of Christ's redeeming love and invitation of mercy, a favorite gospel song from the era of camp meetings and Sunday school revivals.
hymns.lyrics:
Have you heard the story sweet and blest
Of love unmeasured, still, and rest?
How God gave His Son from Heaven above
To tell the wonderful story of love?

Wonderful story of love,
Tell it to me again;
Wonderful story of love,
Write it upon my heart.
hymns.note: Verse/refrain reproduced with moderate confidence; recommend cross-checking exact wording against a hymnal source like Hymnary.org given multiple similarly-titled songs exist.

hymns.title: Ye Must Be Born Again (You Must Be Born Again)
hymns.author_composer: William T. Sleeper (words); George C. Stebbins (music)
hymns.story: Based on Jesus' words to Nicodemus in John 3, this hymn insists plainly that religious ritual or moral effort cannot substitute for the spiritual new birth Christ described, a core evangelical teaching of the revival era.
hymns.lyrics:
A ruler once came to Jesus by night,
To ask Him the way of salvation and light;
The Master made answer in words true and plain,
'Ye must be born again.'

'Ye must be born again, ye must be born again,
I verily, verily, say unto thee,
Ye must be born again.'

Nicodemus was learned and honored and wise,
A teacher of Israel, whom men did not despise;
But the Master he called Him, and Oh, be it plain,
'Ye must be born again.'

Ye children of men, attend to the word
So solemnly uttered by Jesus the Lord,
And let not this message to you be in vain,
'Ye must be born again.'

hymns.title: Hold the Fort
hymns.story: Philip Bliss wrote this after hearing an account (possibly embellished or legendary) of a Civil War general who signaled his besieged troops to hold their position because reinforcements were coming, turning it into a picture of Christians holding firm in faith while awaiting Christ's return.
hymns.lyrics:
Ho, my comrades, see the signal
Waving in the sky!
Reinforcements now appearing,
Victory is nigh!

Hold the fort, for I am coming,
Jesus signals still;
Wave the answer back to Heaven,
By Thy grace we will.

See the mighty host advancing,
Satan leading on;
Mighty men around us falling,
Courage almost gone!

See the glorious banner waving!
Hear the trumpet blow!
In our Leader's Name we'll triumph
Over every foe.

Fierce and long the battle rages,
But our help is near;
Onward comes our great Commander,
Cheer, my comrades, cheer!

hymns.title: Bring Your Vessels, Not a Few
hymns.story: This gospel song draws on the Old Testament story of the widow's oil (2 Kings 4), whose supply of oil only stopped flowing when she ran out of empty vessels to fill - a picture of how much of God's blessing we receive depending on how much room we make for it.
hymns.note: I'm not fully confident in the attribution/date for this title; recommend confirming with Hymnary.org before treating the details above as settled.

hymns.title: Send the Light
hymns.story: Charles Gabriel wrote this as a missionary hymn, urging churches to send the light of the gospel to 'the blessed Gospel light' shining 'across the sea' to people in foreign lands who had not yet heard of Christ, reflecting the strong missions movement of the late 1800s.
hymns.lyrics:
There's a call comes ringing o'er the restless wave,
'Send the light! Send the light!'
There are souls to rescue, there are souls to save,
Send the light! Send the light!

Send the light, the blessed Gospel light;
Let it shine from shore to shore!
Send the light, the blessed Gospel light;
Let it shine forevermore!

We have heard the Macedonian call today,
Send the light! Send the light!
And a golden offering at the cross we lay,
Send the light! Send the light!

Let us pray that grace may everywhere abound,
Send the light! Send the light!
And a Christlike spirit everywhere be found,
Send the light! Send the light!

Let us not grow weary in the work of love,
Send the light! Send the light!
Let us gather jewels for a crown above,
Send the light! Send the light!

hymns.title: Stand Up, Stand Up for Jesus
hymns.story: George Duffield wrote this after his friend and fellow pastor Dudley Tyng died from an accident shortly after preaching a sermon whose final words were 'stand up for Jesus.' Duffield based the hymn's title and theme on those last words as a tribute to his friend.

hymns.title: Only Remembered
hymns.story: Horatius Bonar, a Scottish minister and hymn writer, wrote this on the theme of the fleeting nature of earthly fame, expressing hope that being remembered as one faithful to Christ matters more than worldly recognition.
hymns.lyrics:
Fading away, like the stars of the morning,
Losing their light in the glorious sun,
Thus would we pass from the earth and its toiling,
Only remembered for what we have done.

Only remembered, only remembered,
Only remembered for what we have done;
Thus would we pass from the earth and its toiling,
Only remembered for what we have done.

Fleeting as clouds that swiftly are flying,
Blown by the wind o'er the fair, blue sky,
Thus we pass by, and our names are forgotten,
Only remembered by what we have done.

Only the truth that in life we have spoken,
Only the seed that in life we have sown,
These shall pass onward when we are forgotten,
Fruits of the harvest and what we have done.

hymns.title: There Is a Great Day Coming
hymns.story: Will Thompson, also known for 'Softly and Tenderly,' wrote this hymn as a solemn reminder that a day of judgment is coming for every soul, urging listeners to be ready and to choose which side - salvation or judgment - they will stand on.
hymns.lyrics:
There's a great day coming, a great day coming,
There's a great day coming by and by,
When the saints and the sinners shall be parted right and left,
Are you ready for that day to come?

Are you ready? Are you ready?
Are you ready for the judgment day?
Are you ready? Are you ready?
For the judgment day?

hymns.title: The Last Mile of the Way
hymns.author_composer: Johnson Oatman Jr. (words); George W. Sebren (music)
hymns.story: Another of Johnson Oatman's many gospel hymns, this one comforts believers with the assurance that Christ will personally walk with them through the final, hardest stretch of life's journey into eternity.
hymns.lyrics:
I must go on, in the path I've been going,
I cannot turn from the light I have seen;
I cannot go back to the darkness of nothing,
I must go on where the light has been.

He will be with me, He knows all the way,
Though it be dark as the night;
He will be with me, my hand He will hold,
And give me strength for the fight;
I will not turn from the heavenly way,
He will go with me each step,
And I shall walk with my Lord and my King,
All the last mile of the way.
hymns.note: Verse wording reproduced with lower confidence - the hymn's chorus 'I will walk in the light...all the last mile of the way' is well known but exact verse arrangement varies by hymnal; recommend checking Hymnary.org.

hymns.title: I'll Tell the World That I'm a Christian
hymns.story: This is a joyful testimony hymn in which the singer declares boldly and publicly that they belong to Christ, a favorite in African-American and Southern gospel traditions.
hymns.note: Authorship/date uncertain to me - flagging for verification; copyright status therefore also uncertain.

hymns.title: How Beautiful Heaven Must Be
hymns.story: This gospel hymn imagines the joys awaiting believers in heaven, contrasting the sorrows and toil of earthly life with the promised rest, glory, and reunion with loved ones in the life to come.
hymns.lyrics:
We read of a place that's called heaven,
It's made for the pure and the free;
These truths in God's Word He hath given,
How beautiful heaven must be.

How beautiful heaven must be,
Sweet home of the happy and free;
Fair haven of rest for the weary,
How beautiful heaven must be.

We read of streets there of pure gold,
Of pearly gates, too, we are told;
We'll join in the songs of the ransomed,
How beautiful heaven must be.

Our Savior is now in that city,
And praying that we may come there;
And through all its wonderful glory,
Some mansion for us He'll prepare.
hymns.note: Reproduced with moderate confidence; recommend verifying exact stanza wording against Hymnary.org.

hymns.title: Give Me a Double Portion
hymns.story: I could not confidently identify this exact hymn title. It may reference the Elijah/Elisha story (2 Kings 2, 'a double portion of your spirit') as a chorus theme, but I don't have a specific well-known hymn matching this title with confidence.
hymns.note: Please confirm author/source if you have it.

hymns.title: With Signs Following
hymns.story: I could not confidently identify a widely known hymn under this exact title (it echoes Mark 16:20, 'signs following'), so I don't want to guess at authorship or lyrics.
hymns.note: Please confirm author/source if you have it.

hymns.title: I Am So Glad That Our Father in Heaven
hymns.story: Philip Bliss wrote this simple, tender hymn (often called 'Jesus Loves Even Me') to express, in almost childlike language, wonder and gratitude that God's love extends personally to the singer, not just to humanity in general.
hymns.lyrics:
I am so glad that our Father in heav'n
Tells of His love in the Book He has giv'n;
Wonderful things in the Bible I see,
This is the dearest, that Jesus loves me.

I am so glad that Jesus loves me,
Jesus loves me, Jesus loves me;
I am so glad that Jesus loves me,
Jesus loves even me.

Though I forget Him and wander away,
Still He doth love me wherever I stray;
Back to His dear loving arms do I flee,
When I remember that Jesus loves me.

Oh, if there's only one song I can sing,
When in His beauty I see the great King,
This shall my song in eternity be,
'Oh, what a wonder that Jesus loves me!'

hymns.title: I Know Who Holds Tomorrow
hymns.story: Ira Stanphill, a traveling evangelist and songwriter, wrote this after facing personal heartbreak and an uncertain future in ministry, expressing trust in God even without knowing what the future holds - only that God holds it.
hymns.note: Still under copyright (Ira Stanphill, 1950) - full lyrics not reproduced.

hymns.title: Great Is Thy Faithfulness
hymns.author_composer: Thomas O. Chisholm (words); William M. Runyan (music)
hymns.story: Thomas Chisholm, a Kentucky-born minister who worked much of his life as an insurance agent due to poor health, said the hymn was not born out of any dramatic experience but out of his own quiet, personal gratitude for God's steady faithfulness through the ordinary, unremarkable years of daily life, drawing on Lamentations 3:22-23.

hymns.title: Praise Him! Praise Him!
hymns.author_composer: Fanny J. Crosby (words); Chester G. Allen (music)
hymns.story: Fanny Crosby wrote this joyful hymn of praise to Jesus as 'Redeemer, Friend' - one of hundreds of hymn texts she produced across her long life, often dictating her verses since she was blind from infancy.
hymns.lyrics:
Praise Him! praise Him! Jesus, our blessed Redeemer!
Sing, O earth, His wonderful love proclaim!
Hail Him! hail Him! highest archangels in glory;
Strength and honor give to His holy name!

Praise Him! praise Him! tell of His excellent greatness;
Praise Him! praise Him! ever in joyful song!

Praise Him! praise Him! Jesus, our blessed Redeemer!
For our sins He suffered, and bled, and died;
He our Rock, our hope of eternal salvation,
Hail Him! hail Him! Jesus the Crucified.

Praise Him! praise Him! Jesus, our blessed Redeemer!
Heavenly portals loud with hosannas ring!
Jesus, Savior, reigneth forever and ever;
Crown Him! crown Him! Prophet, and Priest, and King!

hymns.title: A Christian Home
hymns.author_composer: Barbara B. Hart (words); Squire Parsons or traditional tune (varies)
hymns.story: This hymn is a prayer for the home - that it would be a place marked by Christ's presence, love, and peace rather than merely by outward comfort or material success.
hymns.note: Likely still under copyright depending on exact authorship/date - which I'm not fully certain of; lyrics not reproduced out of caution.

hymns.title: Count Your Blessings
hymns.author_composer: Johnson Oatman Jr. (words); Edwin O. Excell (music)
hymns.story: Johnson Oatman wrote this cheerful hymn to encourage discouraged believers to combat despair not by denying their troubles but by deliberately recounting God's blessings, a practical and enduringly popular piece of pastoral counsel set to music.
hymns.lyrics:
When upon life's billows you are tempest tossed,
When you are discouraged, thinking all is lost,
Count your many blessings, name them one by one,
And it will surprise you what the Lord hath done.

Count your blessings, name them one by one;
Count your blessings, see what God hath done!
Count your blessings, name them one by one;
Count your many blessings, see what God hath done.

Are you ever burdened with a load of care?
Does the cross seem heavy you are called to bear?
Count your many blessings, every doubt will fly,
And you will be singing as the days go by.

When you look at others with their lands and gold,
Think that Christ has promised you His wealth untold;
Count your many blessings, money cannot buy
Your reward in heaven, nor your home on high.

So, amid the conflict, whether great or small,
Do not be discouraged, God is over all;
Count your many blessings, angels will attend,
Help and comfort give you to your journey's end.

hymns.title: They That Wait Upon the Lord
hymns.story: This phrase comes from Isaiah 40:31 ('they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength') and is used as a title/theme in several different choruses and anthems, so I can't confidently point to one specific hymn without more detail.
hymns.note: Please let me know the composer or where you encountered this one, if possible, so I can identify the specific version.

compiled_note: Public-domain hymns include full lyrics reconstructed from memory of standard hymnal texts; verse selection/order can vary slightly between hymnals, so cross-check against Hymnary.org for any hymn you plan to print or publish formally. Entries marked identified:false are titles I could not confidently match to a specific known hymn - please provide more detail (composer, a line of lyrics, or where you found the title) so I can fill those in.
